text: Notice that the vectors $$ \evec_1 = \threevec{1}{0}{0}, \evec_2 = \threevec{0}{1}{0}, \evec_3 = \threevec{0}{0}{1} $$ form the columns of the $3\times3$ identity matrix, which implies that this set forms a basis for $\real^3$. More generally, the set of vectors $\evec_1,\evec_2,\ldots,\evec_m$ forms a basis for $\real^m$, which we call the standard basis for $\real^m$.
